bio:
Elise is one of the highest-ranked arms in the class of 2029. She owns the No. 1 ERA in Virginia for her class at 1.30, ranks No. 55 nationally and No. 4 in the Northeast Region in Extra Inning Softball's 2029 pitching rankings, and sits No. 21 nationally on Line Drive Media's Class of 2029 Hot 100.

The numbers hold up across a full year of national competition. In fall 2025 she threw 66.0 innings with 109 strikeouts — 1.65 per inning — against a 1.167 ERA, a .818 WHIP and a .132 opponent average. Over summer 2026 she logged 89.0 innings with 111 strikeouts, a 1.65 ERA, 1.12 WHIP and .186 BAA. She finished tied for 4th on the fall 2025 16U Super Division leaderboard for strikeouts per inning and 4th among Tier 1 pitchers at AFCS Nationals. She works fast, fills the zone, and misses bats without giving away free bases.

At Nansemond-Suffolk Academy she is a two-time VISAA Division II state champion — and as a freshman she was the one who got the ball in the title game. Elise started the 2026 state championship against Christchurch School and went six innings, allowing five hits and three runs, none of them earned, striking out six and walking one in a 7-3 win that gave the Saints their seventh consecutive state title. She had already started the TCIS championship earlier that spring and thrown two no-hit innings with five strikeouts and no walks, then gone 3 2/3 scoreless with five more strikeouts in the VISAA semifinal. A first-team All-State, All-Conference and All-Tidewater selection, she carries a 4.06 GPA with Academic Distinction both semesters and is an Extra Elite Scholar.

bio:
A 2026 NCHSAA 5A state champion as a freshman, Baylee started varsity for Enka High School and led the Sugar Jets in home runs and RBI on their way to the program's fourth state title. Her signature game came in the 5A West Regional Finals, where she hit three home runs — two of them grand slams — in a 12-1 win over North Davidson. In the deciding game of the championship series against West Carteret, her fifth-inning RBI double broke a scoreless tie and sent Enka to a 4-0 win and a 12-game closing streak. She was named to the North Carolina Softball Coaches all-state team as a freshman.

A true utility bat who has played first, third, and the outfield, Baylee carries a 4.3 GPA on an all-honors course load with A honor roll every year since third grade. She plans to study business as a pre-law track toward becoming a family law attorney, and volunteers through Key Club, Special Olympics, and her school's Student Leadership Program.

bio:
On September 29, 2026, Maddie announced her verbal commitment to continue her academic and athletic career playing Division I softball at Elon University. "I'm so excited to call Elon HOME!" she wrote, thanking the Phoenix staff for believing in her and Stars National Walker head coach Joe Walker for four years together: "I wouldn't have wanted to spend the past four years with anyone else. You have helped me grow so much, both on and off the field."

A left-handed slapper and outfielder, Maddie was named to the North Carolina all-state team as a sophomore after helping Weddington complete an undefeated season and win the 7A state championship, delivering hits in key moments of the title series against D.H. Conley. She was also an All-Southern Carolina Conference selection.

Her speed out of the left side puts constant pressure on infield defenses, and her range in the outfield lets her track down balls in the gaps. She has competed in the power and premier pools of top tournaments across the country through the summer circuit.

bio:
A catcher and third baseman at Covenant Day School, Charlotte was a 2026 NCISAA state champion, an all-state honoree, and a first-team all-conference selection as a sophomore. She has been part of a Covenant Day program that put together a five-game win streak including a victory over Charlotte Country Day.

Behind the plate her strong arm and quick release make her a threat to opposing base runners, and her bat provides consistent production in the order. Handling both premium defensive spots — catcher and the hot corner — gives a coaching staff real lineup flexibility. She is a two-year A/B honor roll student (2025, 2026) and a Beta Club member since 2024.
achievements: 2026 Alliance Fastpitch 16U Tier III National Runner-Up

bio:
Cara led all of New York State in both home runs and RBIs in 2026, [slugging 11 home runs as a sophomore](https://www.democratandchronicle.com/picture-gallery/sports/high-school/2026/07/18/meet-the-section-v-athletes-to-watch-in-2026-27/90942192007/) at Pittsford Sutherland with 42 RBIs and a 1.550 OPS. She now holds Sutherland's single-season and career home run records, is on pace to finish among the top five home run hitters in New York State history, and was named third team all-state by the New York State Sportswriters' Association and first team All-Greater Rochester.

The biggest of those swings came in the 2026 postseason: a two-out, three-run home run that broke a scoreless tie and lifted the Knights past Eastridge 5-2 for the Section V Class AA2 championship. She also homered in the 13-1 semifinal rout of Pittsford Mendon, and earlier in the season hit two home runs in a single game. She has led Sutherland in home runs two straight years and finished second in the region last year, and was voted a News 8 WROC athlete of the week by area readers.

A multi-sport athlete with elite speed and competitive fire, Cara is also a varsity ski racer — a 4x sectional champion who placed 5th overall at the 2026 Section V Championships. She brings that same explosiveness to the outfield, with exceptional range and the versatility to contribute in the infield.

bio:
Sophia finished the 2026 high school regular season with the highest batting average in the country. Through Oct. 13 of her junior year at Pueblo Central she was hitting .817 (49-for-60) — first in Colorado across every classification and first on [MaxPreps' national batting-average leaderboard](https://www.maxpreps.com/softball/stat-leaders/) — and had stolen 28 bases in 17 games, second in Class 4A ([ColoradoPreps](https://coloradopreps.com/softball-regular-season-ends-with-standout-statistical-performances/)). The [Pueblo Star Journal](https://pueblostarjournal.org/sport/2026/08/08/fall-high-school-sports-preview-2026/) went into the season calling her "one of the best players in the state."

As a sophomore she hit .560 with six doubles, six triples, a home run, 13 RBI and 17 stolen bases — striking out just three times in 115 plate appearances — and led Colorado in runs scored with 56. At shortstop she turned six double plays with 45 putouts and 47 assists, anchoring a Wildcats team that went 22-6, finished 8-0 in the South-Central League for its second straight league title, and reached the state tournament. She won the league batting title for the second year in a row, was named to the 2025 Colorado all-state team, and was the Pueblo Star Journal's Girls Athlete of the Year for fall 2025. The Pueblo Softball Hall of Fame then named her its [2026 Tony Bobian Memorial Most Valuable High School Player](https://pueblostarjournal.org/sport/2026/05/03/pueblo-softball-hall-of-fame-inducts-new-members-name-high-school-mvp-and-most-valuable-pitcher/).

None of it came out of nowhere. As a freshman she led the South-Central League in batting average (.602), on-base percentage, runs, hits and stolen bases (31) during the regular season and was the only underclassman named All-Conference First Team. She has been Pueblo Central's softball MVP in each of her first two seasons.

She joined Stars National Walker in March 2025 as a left-handed power slapper who can run, and has collected hardware at nearly every stop since: All-Tournament at the 2025 PGF Premier National Championships, and at the 2025 Scenic City Summer event, where Stars reached the 14U championship game out of more than 80 teams; All-Tournament at the 2025 ACFL Fall Championships, where Stars went 6-0 to earn its Alliance Nationals bid; and Offensive Player of the Tournament at the 2025 Veterans Tribute Showcase. She hit .543 with a .588 on-base percentage and did not make an error across the fall 2025 season, then hit .487 with a .569 on-base percentage over 46 games in summer 2026 — closing it on the All-Tournament team at the Alliance Fastpitch Championship Series as Stars finished 16U Tier III National Runner-Up.

Beyond the travel circuit, she has represented Team Mexico at the TCS International Challenge in Colorado two summers running — third place in 2025, runner-up in 2026 — and was selected for the 2026 All World Game. She was invited to the 2026 Colorado All-American All-Star Game and to USA Softball's High Performance Program National Selection Event in Vero Beach, Florida, this December. Extra Inning Softball, where she is a two-year ambassador, ranked her No. 4 in its 2025 regional rankings and named her to its Class of 2028 Mountain Region Standouts list of top-100 hitters.

The speed shows up off the diamond too: she has run 13.01 in the 100 meters for Pueblo Central's track team, where she also runs the 400 and the 4x100 and 4x400 relays, and was named the school's Track Breakout Athlete of the Year in 2025. She has a 51-inch box jump and started for the basketball team as a freshman. In the classroom she carries a 4.0-plus GPA, was inducted into the National Honor Society in 2026, and is an Extra Inning Softball Elite Scholar on its Class of 2028 National Honor Roll. Softball runs in the family — her father, Jeremiah Perez, was inducted into the Pueblo Softball Hall of Fame at the same 2026 ceremony where she received her MVP award, and is an assistant coach with Stars National Walker.

bio:
Contact-first outfielder with plus speed and a plus arm. A multi-sport athlete who competes in outdoor track — triple jump, sprints, and relays — the same explosiveness and top-end speed that make her dangerous on the bases and in the gaps. At the 5A Georgia Meet on Feb. 11, she ran an 8.86 laser-timed 60m, finishing 18th out of 71 competitors. She's also a key leg on her school's 4x100m relay, typically closing the gap as a strong curve runner.

Played the full 2025 summer on an 18U team, traveling the Northeast for major tournaments including TNT and New England's Finest, where she started in center field and hit leadoff all summer. She joined Stars National Walker at PGF Nationals, starting in the outfield and batting .400 for the tournament with multiple stolen bases.

Athletic family: Both parents were student-athletes at the University of Georgia. Dad (Mike) played football; Mom (Karin) was an All-American gymnast.

bio:
Natalie announced herself with a perfect game in her very first varsity start — striking out 14 of the 15 batters she faced in Huntingtown's 20-0 win over Westlake as a freshman. Across her 2026 high school season she threw 16 innings with 35 strikeouts, zero walks, and a 0.00 ERA, allowing just two hits, and batted .471 at the plate. Huntingtown went on to win the Maryland 2A state championship, and in April she was nominated for Maryland softball player of the week.

She carried it straight into summer: across the combined 2026 Stars and Fury travel season she threw 121 innings with 137 strikeouts and batted .575.

A left-handed pitcher and first baseman with elite command, she is a 2026 USA Softball All-American and a Line Drive Media Top 100 player in the Class of 2029. Off the field she carries a 4.1 GPA, made the Honor Roll in 2025 and 2026, and captains her high school volleyball team.

bio:
A sophomore catcher and utility player at Mineral Point, Austyn hit .563 across 31 games in 2026 with a .605 on-base percentage. She finished with 58 hits — 15 doubles and eight home runs — drove in 40 runs, and was a perfect 21-for-21 on stolen bases.

Line Drive Media named her a [2026 1st Team High School All-American catcher](https://linedrivemedia.com/news/high-school-honors-the-2026-live-drive-softball-1st-team-high-school-all-americans-catchers-july-7-2026/). She was also a Line Drive National High School Player of the Week runner-up, plus 1st Team All-District and 1st Team All-State. As a freshman she was 1st Team All-State, All-District, and All-Conference, helping Mineral Point reach the WIAA Division 4 state tournament for the second time in program history — she homered in the sectional final shutout of Waterloo that punched their ticket. Extra Inning Softball rates her a Top 25 Slugger and the No. 100 catcher nationally. She wears #44 for Stars National Walker.
